title: Advertisers are trying to influence AI bots with secret ads
blurb: Advertisers are now serving hidden ads to AI crawlers, embedding content designed to poison model outputs and nudge chatbots toward mentioning their brands when users ask for recommendations. As AI search absorbs more top-of-funnel discovery, this LLM-targeted prompt injection points to a new gray-area channel that could distort AI-generated brand mentions and undermine the organic share-of-voice marketers are starting to track.

title: Solidity Pro VS Code Extensions Steal Crypto Wallets, API Keys, and Credentials
blurb: Malicious VS Code extensions named "Solidity Pro" posed as Solidity developer tooling while harvesting crypto wallet vaults, seed phrases, SSH keys, and API tokens, exfiltrating the data through a Telegram bot. Yeeth Security found the extensions used delayed activation and heavy obfuscation to evade marketplace review, tracing the campaign to the same playbook as the WhiteCobra cluster that pushed Lumma Stealer in 2025.

title: A rare CME shift: Hedge funds abandon structural shorts to bet on a bitcoin rally
blurb: CME leveraged funds have flipped net long on bitcoin futures for the first time in years, abandoning the basis trade after the three-month futures basis fell to roughly 3%, below the 3.8% yield on two-year Treasuries. Bitcoin has rebounded from a July 1 low near $58,000 to above $65,000, and the shift from structural shorts to net long signals institutional traders now positioning for upside.

title: Inside stablecoin firm BVNK’s journey to a $1.8B acquisition by Mastercard
blurb: Mastercard closed its $1.8B acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK, beating out competing bids from Coinbase and Visa despite a reportedly higher Coinbase offer. The deal signals how payments incumbents are racing to lock in positions across the roughly $300B stablecoin market, with Stripe, Visa, and Coinbase all pursuing similar infrastructure plays.

title: Bitcoin hits block 961,632 as the controversial BIP-110 soft fork attempt begins
blurb: Bitcoin reached block 961,632 on Saturday, triggering the mandatory signaling period for BIP-110, a soft fork that would temporarily curb non-financial data embedded on the network, with miner support seldom exceeding 2.5% against the 55% threshold required. Backers are now pushing it as a user-activated soft fork that relies on node operators rejecting non-signaling blocks, raising the prospect of a minority chain splitting from the hashpower-dominant mainnet.

title: Sources: the UK FCA is consulting industry participants, including major banks, on a regulatory framework for tokenized gold; London dominates the global market (Financial Times)
blurb: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority is consulting industry participants, including major banks, on a regulatory framework for tokenized gold, according to the Financial Times. London's dominance of the global physical gold market gives the effort outsized weight, positioning the UK to set early standards for onchain commodity settlement before the US or EU move.

title: Hyperliquid’s RWA perps boom is eating into the revenue that backs HYPE
blurb: Hyperliquid's gross protocol revenue has fallen 43% from its Q3 2025 peak of ~$357M to ~$202M in Q2 2026, even as 30-day perp volume hit ~$178B and open interest set a 2026 high above $11B. The gap traces to HIP-3, which lets builders who stake 500,000 HYPE deploy their own markets and keep up to half the fees, and those builder-deployed markets now account for roughly half of platform volume.

title: Live updates: BTC above $65,000 even as the Senate punts the CLARITY Act to the fall
blurb: Bitcoin held near $65,200 on Monday, up 3.7% on the week, even after the Senate fell nine votes short on the CLARITY Act and pushed any market-structure action to September 14 at the earliest. Spot ETFs strung together consecutive days of inflows and a softer dollar since the weak US jobs report drove the bid, with strategists arguing the CLARITY delay was already priced in.

title: Bitcoin investors pour $853 million into spot ETFs. BlackRock’s IBIT claims the bulk
blurb: Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded $853M in net inflows in the week ended Aug. 7, the strongest week since April, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for $693M of it. The ETFs remain roughly $4.5B in the red year-to-date, so sustained weekly inflows above $1B, the pace that drove 2025's rally, would be needed to fuel a meaningful price move.

title: Is Clarity's delay a blessing in disguise?: State of Crypto
blurb: The Senate will not hold a procedural vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act before its August recess, pushing any action on the bill to mid-September at the earliest and dimming its odds of becoming law this year. CoinDesk argues the delay may help crypto, since a failed cloture vote could have killed the bill until the next Congress amid unresolved fights over Trump's crypto ties and stablecoin yields.

title: Robinhood brings crypto trading to UK in AI-powered all-in-one app
blurb: Robinhood launched zero-fee crypto trading in the UK, giving customers access to over 50 tokens including Bitcoin alongside stocks and shares ISAs, equities, options, and futures inside its all-in-one app. The rollout also brings Robinhood Cortex Digests for Crypto, a generative AI widget that explains price drivers in plain English, and opens its Arbitrum-based Robinhood Chain L2 to UK developers.

title: Crypto is going through a massive dot-com style shakeout as over 100 projects fold in 2026
blurb: Over 100 crypto projects have shut down, filed for bankruptcy or gone dark in 2026, per RootData, with BitMEX, BitMart, Movement Labs, and Storj Labs all exiting in a single week as altcoins fell 70% to 90% and drained token-denominated treasuries. Survivors like Aave, Hyperliquid, and Ether.fi are those charging fees in stablecoins or cash rather than relying on speculative token distribution.

title: Hardware wallet sales in Russia more than double as new crypto rules near
blurb: Russian consumer demand for hardware crypto wallets more than doubled in the first half of 2026, with M.Video reporting a 107% jump in Q2 unit sales over Q1 and Wildberries an 84% year-on-year rise. The buying precedes Russia's new crypto regime taking effect Sept. 1, which permits regulated exchanges and caps retail purchases of liquid assets at 300,000 rubles annually per intermediary.

title: Sources: the UK FCA is consulting industry participants, including major banks, on a regulatory framework for tokenized gold; London dominates the global market (Financial Times)
blurb: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority is consulting banks and other industry participants on a regulatory framework for tokenized gold, according to the Financial Times. London already dominates the global gold market, and clear rules on tokenized reserves would give the FCA an early lead in setting standards for a fast-growing corner of real-world-asset tokenization.

title: Inside stablecoin firm BVNK’s journey to a $1.8B acquisition by Mastercard
blurb: Mastercard closed its $1.8B acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK, beating out competing bids from Coinbase and Visa despite Coinbase reportedly offering more. The deal reflects how Stripe, Visa, Mastercard, and Coinbase are racing to lock up positions in the roughly $300B stablecoin market, with incumbent networks buying rails rather than building them.

title: Revolut clinches French banking licence
blurb: Revolut secured a French banking licence from the ACPR and the ECB, adding to its Lithuanian-issued European licence and clearing the way to offer locally tailored products like loans to its 30M Western European customers. The approval follows last year's ECB restrictions over Revolut's product-approval controls and precedes a €1B regional investment and a Paris HQ, with customers migrating to the new licence starting in France.

title: India’s UPI Payments Developer Targets Diaspora For Growth
blurb: NPCI, the operator of India's UPI real-time payments network, plans to expand globally by targeting the country's overseas diaspora as a beachhead for cross-border transactions. The move positions UPI to compete with correspondent-banking rails and remittance incumbents on the corridors where Indian expats send money home, pressuring settlement costs and timing in one of the world's largest remittance markets.

title: Rakuten Earns First Profit in Six Years With Fintech Boost
blurb: Rakuten Group posted its first quarterly net income in six years, driven by growth in its fintech and e-commerce segments. The result underscores how Rakuten's payments, banking, and credit-card arms have become the profit engine offsetting years of losses from its mobile-carrier buildout.

title: Robinhood brings crypto trading to UK in AI-powered all-in-one app
blurb: Robinhood launched zero-fee crypto trading in the UK, adding over 50 tokens to an all-in-one app that already carries stocks-and-shares ISAs, equities, options, and futures. The rollout bundles Cortex Digests for Crypto, a generative-AI widget that reads news and market data to explain price moves in plain English, positioning Robinhood against incumbent UK platforms that lean on wide spreads.

title: DORA Is No Longer a Deadline
blurb: The European Supervisory Authorities published their first DORA incident overview on June 3, 2026, ending the informal supervisory tolerance of 2025 as national authorities begin auto-cross-checking Register of Information submissions and issuing initial compulsion payments. Enforcement is arriving unevenly, with penalty ceilings ranging from Italy's €20M or 10% of turnover down to the Czech Republic's €2M, even as Poland and Bulgaria have yet to fully transpose DORA into national law.

title: How credit card issuers and reservation apps like OpenTable and Amex-owned Resy fragment restaurant reservations, wiring the best tables into premium card perks (Wall Street Journal)
blurb: Credit card issuers and reservation platforms including OpenTable and Amex-owned Resy are wiring the best restaurant tables into premium card perks, fragmenting availability across booking apps tied to specific cards. The shift turns dining reservations into a customer-acquisition and retention lever for issuers, deepening the link between high-annual-fee cards and exclusive access as premium-card competition intensifies.
